text: Auto-drill research complete. Build one over rich ground, and let it collect ore while you plan the next step.
Conveyors ready. Connect a drill to the machine that needs its output. Your backpack may finally have a quiet afternoon.
Power pylons ready. Link them to your existing network before building machines farther from the shelter.
Storage silos ready. Give your belts somewhere to deliver spare materials. The floor has served admirably, but lacks organisation.
Coal power is available. It works through the night, but the smoke is a cost. Keep improving your solar supply.
Silicon furnace ready. Feed it silica and carbon, then use the silicon to research better equipment.
Four more backpack slots. A remarkable advance in the science of putting things somewhere.
Drill upgrade complete. Your auto-drills work faster now. Check that their belts and storage can keep up.
Solar output improved. Your lotuses make more power in daylight. Keep enough battery storage for the night.
Electrolyzer placed. Give it ice and power near the shelter. Water supplies the oxygen; electricity does the separating.
Battery placed. Let spare power charge it before sunset. An empty battery is chiefly an optimistic box.
Solar lotus placed. Daylight becomes electricity. Pair it with a battery to keep useful work going after sunset.
Smelter placed. Load iron ore and carbon, and check its power supply. Iron plates come with smoke; plan accordingly.
Research station placed. Choose a project and load its parts. It will need power while it works.
Auto-drill placed. Check the resource beneath it, then arrange a belt or regular collection for its output.
Storage silo placed. Connect an incoming belt to store materials, and an outgoing belt when another machine needs them.
Pylon placed. Check its connection to a powered network. A tall pole cannot generate electricity through confidence alone.
Coal burner placed. Carbon will keep it running after sunset. Watch the air as carefully as the power meter.
Silicon furnace placed. It needs silica, carbon and power. The silicon will help improve your drills, backpack and solar cells.
First belt connected. Check the receiving machine has room and the right inputs. One moving item is a promising start.
The drill has filled its output space. Empty it or connect a belt so it can get back to work.
This machine is outside your power network. Move it closer, or extend a connected line of pylons to reach it.
Oxygen below twenty-five percent. Get to the shelter, or breathe a canister with Q.
You blacked out. I carried you back to the shelter. Please do not make me do that again.
The sun is setting. Solar output dropping.
Sunrise. Solar power returning.
Your backpack is full. Craft something, or we will need machines to carry more.
Not here — I will not let you dig under the shelter.
Research complete:
That machine has no power. Build it within 30 m of the shelter, or carry power out with pylons.
A drill is full and has stopped. Empty it, or give it a belt.
Acid rain is getting into the machines. Walk up to any that need attention and press E.
The forest is thriving. Look — blooms are opening.
The air is getting heavier. The forest is holding on.
The forest is wilting and the rain is turning sour. Build filters, or slow the smelters.
Jivagraha is struggling to breathe. Something deep below is restless.
A bloom. It grew because the world is clean. Research can use it.
The hatch is responding. Take one breath, then follow the daylight.
The shelter is sound, but its tank is empty. There is ice in the rocks nearby. Use your laser.
Good. Ice gives us water, and water gives us air. We need iron to build the machine that splits it.
Sandstone is mostly silica. Dig into the ground below the grass — I will count what you collect.
You have everything for an electrolyzer. It splits ice into oxygen and hydrogen.
Set it close to the shelter so its air pipes reach inside.
The solar lotus will power it while the sun is up.
Electrolysis complete. You are breathing. I consider that a good start.
Night is coming. Solar power will fall to zero. I recommend a battery. And perhaps a blanket.
The forest is glowing. I have never seen anything like it. Or… I do not remember seeing it.
Iron plates mean real machines. Careful — smelting makes smoke, and this world notices.
Carrying everything by hand will not scale. A research station can work out machines that do it for us.
Give the station the parts it asks for. It needs power while it thinks.
The drill mines whatever is under it. Iron veins run in thin stripes; look for rich ground.
A drill that nobody empties will fill up and stop. We need belts.
A belt from the drill to the smelter, and the smelter never waits for you again.
Iron plates, made while you were not looking. I believe this is called a factory.
Return to the module and listen to Prof. Huxley's recording by the hatch. The factory can manage a short absence.
Collect the translator beside the escape module, as Prof. Huxley suggested.
Follow the blue beams to find three memory logs scattered by the crash and read each one.
Our machines make smoke and stir up mud. The planet notices. Look at it from above.
Seismic tremor beneath the forest. The ground shifted, but the trees have not fallen.
Hold Scan beside the valley to trace the roots beneath our drills.
Move every drill away from the marked roots so they have room to settle.
Supply bio-filters near the smog with water and power until the haze clears.
Replant bloom spores around the exposed roots once the soil is clean, then give the new growth time to settle.
Stay a moment. The roots are loosening.
With Mooladri calm, Jivagraha's flora now absorbs pollution twice as quickly. An excellent arrangement for everyone.
Cryo-pod seals hiss open. Custodian, our escape module has crashed, and you are awake. Welcome back.
Systems online. Your memory may take a moment to settle. My filing system has not enjoyed the landing either.
Your suit oxygen is low. Please check the gauge before leaving the pod.
The module has limited reserves. We need a steady oxygen supply before they run out.
I can see a shelter dome outside, beside a solar lotus. Both may still be useful.
The hatch is responding. Take one breath, then follow the daylight.
The hatch is open. Sunrise is rolling over a curved horizon. This is a very small world.
Seismic tremor beneath the forest. The ground shifted, but the trees have not fallen.
A vast shadow is moving beneath those roots. The whole canopy is rising and settling with it.
Mooladri's roots are tightening around the valley. The forest is dimming as our machines strain its home.
Mooladri has risen. Mossy bark towers above us, its crown of glowing root tips brightening. Living roots have closed the valley.
We can help the valley recover. First, we need to learn where Mooladri's roots run.
Use a seismic scan beside the valley. It will trace the living roots beneath our drills.
The root map is clear. Move the drills away from every marked root before we continue.
The drills are clear. Mooladri's roots have loosened, but the haze remains.
Place working bio-filters near the smog and give the air time to clear.
The haze is thinning. Light is returning to the forest, and Mooladri's crown is steadier.
The soil is clean now. Replant the bloom spores around Mooladri's exposed roots.
The bloom has taken root. The ground is settling, and new growth is spreading between the old roots.
Mooladri has settled into the forest. The roots have opened a path into the valley.
With Mooladri calm, Jivagraha's flora now absorbs pollution twice as quickly. An excellent arrangement for everyone.
There is a chamber below this seam. Its light does not match the minerals around it.
I am detecting a signal consistent with a Quantum Fragment. We need a closer reading before I can confirm it.
Roots thread along the chamber wall. The forest appears to have grown around whatever lies below.
We cannot reach the chamber safely yet. Let us finish our work above ground and return.
Starter ship ready. Hydrogen and oxygen are flowing to the engines, and the cargo is secure.
The launch pad is clear. Our first voyage will be short, provided the navigation system remembers its job.
We are rising above Jivagraha. From here, the shelter is a speck and the forest is a ring of light.
Our next destination is Taptashila, a mineral-rich world closer to the sun. We will need better shielding there.
Taptashila is coming into view. I am reading something unusual beneath its oldest rock. We have another question to answer.
Give that grazer space to feed and watch it from here. We can be interesting from a distance.
Stand back from that small opening and watch the burrower look around. Our welcome appears to be provisional.
Look above the forest for a small bird circling in daylight. A useful reminder to look up occasionally.
Pause and leave the grazer room to wander; it steps away when we come too close.
Step back from the burrower's opening and wait quietly. It has concluded this meeting.
Give the bird's roost some space as dusk falls. Its working day appears to be over.
Follow the daylight through the open hatch to the shelter beside the solar lotus.
Gather blue ice, rust-red iron and silica beneath the grass, then press Tab to craft an electrolyzer.
Place a battery on the shelter's power network before sunset and let spare solar power charge it. Darkness accepts no promises.
Load the powered smelter with iron ore and carbon, then walk close to collect its finished plates.
Research drills and conveyors at a powered station, then press C, click the drill, then click the smelter.
Look for Prof. Huxley's recording on the main deck and press E to listen.
Search the front deck for the translator Prof. Huxley mentioned.
Read any memory log you find with E, then press J to revisit it in the Codex.
Check the vehicle bay's parts list and supply what is missing to finish the rover. Your boots have earned some assistance.
Use a seismic scan beside the valley, then move every drill away from the marked living roots.
Keep bio-filters near the smog supplied with water and power until the haze clears.
Replant bloom spores around Mooladri's exposed roots once the soil is clean, then give the new growth time to settle.
Follow the path Mooladri has opened and scan the unfamiliar light below the seam when the chamber is safely reachable.
Check the launch pad's parts list, gather what is missing, and choose a clear site for assembly.
Finish the ship's listed parts, supply hydrogen and oxygen, and check its cargo before launch.
Complete the launch checks and begin lift-off once the pad is clear. My navigation system is preparing its best effort.
Gather blue ice, rust-red iron and silica beneath the grass, then tap Bag to craft an electrolyzer.
Research drills and conveyors at a powered station, then tap Belt, then Pick on the drill, then Pick on the smelter.
Look for Prof. Huxley's recording on the main deck and tap Use to listen.
Read any memory log you find with Use, then tap Codex to revisit it.
